subtopics.title: The Working Tool — Two Points and One Equality

questions.question: The working equality for conservation of mechanical energy compares:
options: The forces at two points of the motion
Kinetic plus potential energy at one point with kinetic plus potential at another
The times taken along two different paths
The accelerations at the top and bottom

questions.question: The reference level (h = 0) is best placed:
options: At the lower of your two chosen points, so no height goes negative

questions.question: At the very peak of a ball's vertical flight, for an instant:
options: E k is zero, because the speed is zero
E k equals E p exactly

questions.question: The energy equality never needs which piece of information?
options: The heights of the two points
The object's speeds at the points
The time taken and the shape of the path

subtopics.title: Straight Up and Straight Down — Throws and the Pendulum

questions.question: A ball is thrown straight up at 14 m/s (no air resistance). Using ½v² = gh, it rises:
Without air resistance, the speed at any height going up compared with the same height coming down is:
options: Exactly equal — the journeys are mirror images

questions.question: A pendulum bob is released 0,45 m above its lowest point. Its speed at the bottom is √(2 × 9,8 × 0,45), which equals:
The bob swings up the far side and rises to exactly its release height because:
options: Gravity switches off at the bottom
It has no energy to buy any extra height

subtopics.title: The Roller Coaster — Working the Big One

questions.question: The 500 kg car crosses the 20 m crest at 4 m/s. Its mechanical energy there is:
At the bottom of the hill, 250v² = 102 000 gives a speed of:
Forgetting the car's 4 000 J of crest kinetic energy produces:
options: A speed that is far too large
A wrong but plausible-looking 19,80 m/s — the classic trap

questions.question: At 8 m on the descent, E k = 102 000 − 39 200 = 62 800 J, so the speed is:

subtopics.title: Inclined Planes and the Independence of Path

questions.question: A rider starts from rest atop a 3,2 m water slide (no friction). Arrival speed is √(2 × 9,8 × 3,2), which equals:
A steep slide and a long gentle flume drop the same 3,2 m. Compared with the flume rider, the steep-slide rider arrives:
options: Sooner, but at exactly the same speed
At the same time but faster
Slower, because the drop is more sudden

questions.question: "The path can be ignored" means the ledger prices only:
options: The track's length and its angle
The time taken and the curve radius
The object's height and its speed

questions.question: At Grade 10, when a question includes friction, you are expected to:
options: Use E k1 + E p1 = E k2 + E p2 anyway
Reason that mechanical energy decreased and transferred to heat — not calculate the loss

questions.question: On a frictionless swing, your speed is greatest:
options: At the very bottom of the arc
At the top of the far side

questions.question: The far side of the swing lifts you to:
options: Slightly higher than your release height
Exactly your release height — no trade can leave you richer
A height that depends on your mass

questions.question: An unpushed swing gradually dies down because:
options: Air resistance withdraws a little energy as heat on every pass

questions.question: Two riders leave the same 3,2 m height from rest on differently shaped slides (no friction). At the pool:
options: The steeper slide's rider is moving faster
The longer slide's rider is moving faster
The heavier rider is moving faster
Both are moving at the same 7,92 m/s

questions.question: The energy method beats the equations of motion on curved paths because it needs:
options: Only a starting balance of energy — no straight line, no constant acceleration
The exact shape of the curve

questions.question: The coaster car was moving at 4 m/s over the crest. Its 4 000 J of kinetic energy must be:
options: Ignored, since it is small compared with 98 000 J
Counted in the total — the ledger counts every coin carried over the crest

subtopics.title: Why the Second Hill Is Always Lower

questions.question: The first hill of a roller coaster is the tallest because:
options: It looks most impressive from the queue
Later hills would block the view
The car's entire energy budget is banked at the first crest
The chain motor works better at the start

questions.question: On a real track, each later hill is lower by MORE than sealed-account arithmetic requires because:
options: Friction takes a toll on every metre of track
Passengers get heavier during the ride

questions.question: A ball thrown up at 14 m/s returns to the hand (no air resistance) moving at:
options: Exactly 14 m/s — perfect trade out, perfect trade back

questions.question: The phrase that seals the account and licenses the conservation equality is:
